verdict.root_cause: Frontend's own request handling, error rate and downstream span timings are all normal or better than baseline; what is anomalous is a cluster of outbound gRPC client failures (status 14 UNAVAILABLE) whose newest lines attribute the failure to DNS name resolution failing for the adservice target on port 9555 [tr_c27c47009e12]. The connection is never established, so adservice is either not resolvable or has no healthy endpoints behind its name — a dependency-availability/discovery fault on the adservice path, not a frontend fault. No change record exists for frontend or checkoutservice to anchor this to a deploy or edit [tr_b4f84b5748b1][tr_d6f70a4c5c7c], and the alert at 04:06 is not corroborated by any error-ratio transition at frontend or loadgenerator [tr_1e14b9d3d52c][tr_88dbd8dfe2d2], so the impact is partial (ad panel) rather than a full outage.
verdict.reasoning: Logs are the only dispatch that found a live anomaly, and it is frontend-as-client failing to resolve adservice [tr_c27c47009e12]. Traces show frontend reaching productcatalogservice and cartservice with sub-millisecond backend spans and no errored spans, so the failure is confined to a path not exercised in those samples [tr_0fadf4f5fafb]. Frontend and loadgenerator error ratios are below baseline with no change point at 04:06 [tr_1e14b9d3d52c][tr_88dbd8dfe2d2], consistent with a non-critical dependency failing closed. Empty change logs remove deploy/config-edit anchors for the two services queried [tr_b4f84b5748b1][tr_d6f70a4c5c7c]. I cannot distinguish 'adservice pods gone/unready' from 'cluster DNS broken' from this evidence, so fault_class stays unknown rather than being forced into bad_config.
open_questions: Is adservice running with ready endpoints, or is cluster DNS itself failing? No adservice-side metrics, logs or change history were pulled.
What actually fired the 04:06 alert? No frontend or loadgenerator metric shows a transition there, and no latency series was ever returned [tr_1e14b9d3d52c].
Traces cover only ~16s at 04:07:42-04:07:58 with no 04:06 coverage and no adservice span [tr_0fadf4f5fafb], so the onset minute is unobserved.

alternatives.root_cause: Cluster DNS/service-discovery is degraded, and adservice is merely the first name whose resolution failed.
alternatives.why_not: Only the adservice target appears in the failing lines; calls to productcatalogservice and cartservice resolved and completed normally [tr_0fadf4f5fafb], which argues against a broad resolver outage.

alternatives.root_cause: A wrong adservice address/port value in frontend's environment points at a name that does not resolve.
alternatives.why_not: No config edit is recorded for frontend in the window [tr_b4f84b5748b1], and similar UNAVAILABLE errors appear as far back as 03:10 [tr_c27c47009e12], inconsistent with a single wrong value introduced at onset.

proposal.expected_effect: Recreating adservice should re-register its name/endpoint so frontend can resolve adservice:9555. Confirm by: the repeating 'status 14 UNAVAILABLE / DNS resolution failed for adservice:9555' lines in {service="frontend"} in Loki ceasing, and adservice spans reappearing under frontend spans in Tempo. Frontend error ratio is not a valid signal - it never moved with the fault.
proposal.if_wrong: If the frontend DNS-failure log lines continue at the same cadence after adservice is confirmed recreated and running, the fault is the resolver/service-discovery layer, not adservice process state, and no permitted action addresses it. If adservice is found already running and ready, the process-state premise was wrong. Note: no adservice-side metric, log or change evidence was ever pulled, so this rests on a caller-side inference only.
proposal.risk: Irreversible recreate that discards adservice in-process cache; if the real fault is cluster DNS, the restart fixes nothing, adds a cold-start gap in ad serving, and destroys the pre-restart process state that would have distinguished the two hypotheses.
proposal.blast_radius: adservice only, for the duration of the recreate. Frontend is its caller and will see continued or briefly worsened ad-panel failures; user-visible impact stays partial (ad panel). No effect expected on cartservice, productcatalogservice, checkoutservice, recommendationservice or loadgenerator.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical alerts on frontend plus the load generator indicate user-facing failure, not an isolated synthetic blip, and no open incident covers it. Cause is undetermined; frontend's five dependencies are the natural first sweep.
